I'm a 42-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with a university degree in agriculture. I returned to farming five years ago after working in Shijiazhuang for over a decade, so I have the textbook knowledge but only five seasons of my own fields to calibrate it against. My wife works at the township primary school, and with two kids still at home, our household has steady off-farm income — but that also means family labor is tight during peak periods. On just 6 mu, I can't rely on economies of scale; I have to maximize yield per mu and manage my time precisely.

For **winter wheat**, I'm targeting about 500 kg per mu. I had the soil tested two years ago — organic matter is moderate, pH around 7.8 — so I need roughly 20 kg N per mu to hit that yield without excessive waste. I split the nitrogen three ways: about 8 kg N as compound fertilizer in the base before planting, 7 kg N as urea at jointing in early April, and another 5 kg N at heading if the crop color indicates it needs a boost. I'm also applying 6 kg P₂O₅ and 5 kg K₂O as base. I plant around October 8th with an improved variety — not saved seed — because uniform germination matters for my plant population target. I irrigate three times: freezing water in late November, jointing in late March, and grain filling in mid-May. Electricity for the well pump runs about 30 yuan per mu per irrigation, so wheat irrigation alone is 540 yuan, but the marginal return on that third irrigation at grain filling is worth it based on my records. I hire four days of labor for wheat planting and harvest because my wife and I are both working during those weeks.

For **summer maize**, the turnaround after wheat harvest is brutal — sometimes only three or four days. I plant immediately after harvest, around June 10th-12th, using Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed at about 90 yuan per mu. I do minimal tillage, maybe one quick pass with the rotary tiller if the stubble is thick, then plant right away. I put 10 kg N as compound fertilizer in the seed furrow at planting, then side-dress 8 kg N as urea at the big trumpet stage around late July. That side-dressing is critical — in my third year I skipped it to save time and lost nearly 80 kg per mu. I also apply 5 kg P₂O₅ and 4 kg K₂O as base. I irrigate twice: once at seedling stage if June is dry, and once at flowering in early August, which is the most water-sensitive period. I use herbicide at planting and monitor for insects, applying insecticide only if I see damage. I hire three days of labor for maize planting and harvest.

Total input costs this year come to about 4,600 yuan. That's a significant share of my expected revenue from 6 mu, but with our off-farm income we can afford the inputs, and on a small plot cutting corners costs more than it saves. I keep about 3,000 yuan in reserve for emergencies — a habit from my city years.
